title: Interteam dependency staircase: sequencing, ownership, and contingency playbook
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a prescriptive, lightweight playbook (the 'Dependency Staircase') that surface, sequences, and operationalizes cross-team dependencies across Engineering, Design, Security, and Infra so roadmap cutovers meet SLAs and launch windows.

Context: Roadmap delivery slippage is frequently caused by unclear ownership, late discovery of security/infrastructure blockers, and misaligned sequencing between feature work and infra preparations (Dedicated/Private rollout prerequisites). Current dependency artifacts are ad hoc (spreadsheets, channel threads) and lack automated readiness signals or contingency lanes. This ticket defines the playbook, scorecard signals, tooling integration points, and initial rollout across three teams as a pilot.

Scope:
- Define the staircase model: Ready -> Guardrails -> Contingency Lane -> Escalation.
- Specify ownership model per dependency (requester, blocking team, tracer).
- Create a scorecard of readiness signals (API contract approved, infra quota allocated, security checklist complete, design signoff, e2e smoke tests passing).
- Map common dependency archetypes (infra capacity, security review, UX consent flow, model tuning) to staircase lanes and SLAs.
- Build Linear templates and Slack alert rules to automate state transitions and highlight falling-through items on roadmap boards.
- Produce a rollout plan and training for three pilot initiatives (Dedicated autoscaling controls, Console rollout, Private VPC onboarding).

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook doc published in Confluence with examples and decision matrix.
- Linear custom field/template available and in use by pilot teams.
- Three pilot initiatives onboarded and scored weekly for 6 weeks.
- At least one automation reduces manual triage time (measured by time from dependency creation to owner ack) by 30% in pilot.
- Escalation flow successfully used in a simulated cutover exercise.

Success metrics:
- Mean time to acknowledgement for cross-team dependency <= 48 hours.
- % of roadmap items with explicit 'staircase lane' and owner >= 95% for pilot initiatives.
- Reduction in blocked days attributable to cross-team handoff by 20% quarter-over-quarter.

Tradeoffs / constraints:
- We must balance playbook rigor with lightweight adoption; initial release should avoid heavy gating that slows small, fast-moving teams.
- Automation scope limited in Q1: start with Linear templates + Slack webhooks before investing in full API-driven orchestration.
- Some security reviews require manual evidence and cannot be fully automated; we will standardize artifacts to speed review.

Risks:
- Cultural resistance if the playbook feels like added process. Mitigation: run shadowing sessions and adopt a 'coach' model during pilot.
- Tooling mismatches between teams (different Linear workflows). Mitigation: provide mapping table and minimal required fields.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Week 1-2: Draft playbook, define signals, produce Linear template.
2) Week 3: Run training with pilot teams; enable Slack alerts and create a monitoring dashboard.
3) Weeks 4-9: Pilot runs with weekly reviews and rapid adjustments.
4) Week 10: Conduct simulated cutover exercise and measure metrics.
5) Week 11-12: Iterate on playbook and plan wider rollout.

Owners: PM: Diego Romero (owner of playbook), Eng lead: Priya Nair (ENG-31824), Design liaison: Marco Li (DES-4412), Security liaison: Evan Hughes (SEC-2043), Infra liaison: Hanna Berg (INF-1782).

Open questions:
- Which readiness signals can be reliably surfaced from CI and infra dashboards versus manual checklists? (Action: spike to catalogue signals by Week 1).
- What SLAs for escalation are acceptable for enterprise customers? (Action: coordinate with Sales/CS).
- Do we require a separate SLA tier for Dedicated vs Hosted API launches?

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/Dependency+Staircase+Playbook
- Linear template (design doc link): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c4-dep-template
- Monitoring dashboard (prototype): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dep-staircase/overview
- Simulation runbook (doc): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/Dependency+Cutover+Simulation

Notes: This playbook intentionally focuses on high-value, repeatable dependency types (security gating, infra capacity, design signoff, model onboarding). The objective is to make cross-team dependencies visible early and provide clear, automated handoffs and contingency options so roadmap commitments are predictable.
